answer.rationale: Symptoms point most strongly at the release 2 hours ago: p99 on the write path began climbing 90 minutes after deploy and correlates temporally with the rollout. Rollback (memory_b1) is proven to clear regressions quickly without customer impact and does not risk in-flight settlement writes. Regional failover (memory_b2) fits the primary-region confinement, but failing over during the daily settlement write peak risks losing or duplicating in-flight writes, which violates the primary objective; it also would not help if the release itself is the cause, since the bad build would follow traffic. Capacity, circuit breakers, and read replicas do not address the write path. Verifying memory_b1 confirms rollback mechanics/safety before committing the single intervention. If post-rollback latency does not recover, failover becomes the next-window candidate.
